- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- Model often lags mean reversion by 3–7 days; if sentiment shows reversal (e.g., +0.2 to -0.4), adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average to avoid overreach.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.2 to 0.4 spikes, model tends to overshoot; apply 1–2% downward correction after 3 consecutive positive sentiment days.
